```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is one paying customer within 90 days. A names a specific buyer pair, a Wisconsin public adjuster and an affiliated roofing contractor. B has no identified buyer and depends on cold discovery in a crowded App Store, where its own brief calls discovery the bottleneck.",
    "B's core use case, plain description generation, is now free through Shopify Magic for every paid-plan merchant. That undercuts the 'merchants without a copywriter' segment. A has no comparable free substitute in its brief.",
    "A's price anchors are well sourced at roughly $65–$250/mo per firm (ClaimWizard, claimOS, Claim Titan, AdjustCRM). B's sourced comparables run as low as $5–$19/mo entry tiers, so far fewer dollars come from each hard-won customer.",
    "B's evidence suggests new entrants struggle: Descrii has 0 reviews, Gelo.ai has 3, and Describly has one 1-star review. B also flags that the need may be one-time per catalog, which threatens recurring payment.",
    "A's main risks bear more on scale than on a first sale. These are the 188-licensee Wisconsin market and the larger build scope. The Wisconsin data-security and breach-notification obligations are a real but bounded hurdle before live claimant PII is handled."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "The ADA urgency claim, which cites $25,000–$75,000 alt-text settlements and says 77% of ADA lawsuits target online stores. It comes from vendor marketing blogs (goodysell.com, compliapoint.com) that have an interest in selling accessibility services. No primary legal source is given. It is also offered as urgency, not as evidence that merchants will pay for this specific app.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A's edge rests mostly on the existence of a named customer. The brief leaves that customer's commitment as an open question ('real/recurring or informal?'). A's quoted demand evidence comes from other firms (a Florida PA and a Reddit user), not the named customer. If that relationship is informal, A's advantage narrows considerably, though B's free-native-substitute problem would still weigh against it."
}
```
